# Refrigeration Cycle

(Heat Pump)

A refrigeration cycle uses work to move heat from a cold region to a warm one; the vapor-compression cycle does it by evaporating a refrigerant at low pressure, compressing it, condensing it at high pressure, and expanding it through a throttling valve.

Its performance is measured by the coefficient of performance, for a refrigerator and COPR=QL/W\text{COP}_R = Q_L/W for a heat pump, which uses the same cycle to heat. The Carnot limit COPHP=QH/W=COPR+1\text{COP}_{HP} = Q_H/W = \text{COP}_R + 1 shows that performance falls as the temperature lift grows: COPR=TL/(TH−TL)\text{COP}_R = T_L/(T_H - T_L) K and TL=270T_L = 270 K allow at most TH=310T_H = 310. Real systems reach a half or less of the limit. Control of refrigeration and heat pump systems regulates evaporator superheat with expansion valves and capacity with variable-speed compressors.6.756.75

## Lessons

parallel-fast.snippet: Steady state and dynamic simulation and optimization are a key step in the design of heating, ventilation, air- conditioning and refrigeration (HVAC&R) systems. It is well known that the computation time in such simulations is dominated by the refrigerant thermophysical property calculations. These calculations generally involve calculating all thermophysical properties given one or two independent parameters. Refrigerant thermophysical properties are typically calculated using some fundamental equations of state (EOS). The NIST REFPROP database is an industrially accepted standard for EOS implementation. Due to the iterative nature of the EOS calculations in REFPROP, the computation time is significant and sometimes not acceptable for optimization of HVAC&R systems.
